title: Developer Session Cost Forecasting SDK PRD
author: Evelyn Chen
content:
Overview

Purpose
This Product Requirements Document defines the Developer Session Cost Forecasting SDK (DSC-SDK), a lightweight client library and reference implementation that enables Redwood customers and partner engineering teams to estimate per-session and per-route expected inference cost before invoking live inference.

Executive summary
Many early-stage integrations underspend time and effort because engineering teams cannot easily predict how different usage shapes (prompt length, streaming vs batch, embedding retention) map to unit costs and latency. The DSC-SDK provides in-app cost forecasts, what-if simulations, and a configurable policy layer so product teams can: (1) simulate cost for traffic profiles, (2) instrument preflight cost checks in developer sandboxes, and (3) feed forecasts into client-side routing/feature gating.

Scope and intended audience
- Primary: SDK consumers (frontend/backend engineers) integrating Redwood inference into product flows.
- Secondary: Solutions engineers, CS, and partner integrators using the reference app for onboarding.

Goals and success metrics
- Developer adoption: 25% of new self-serve signups integrate DSC-SDK into their sandbox within 90 days of GA.
- Forecast accuracy: median forecast error <= 12% across our top 10 model variants and common traffic profiles (90th percentile error <= 25%).
- Latency: SDK library adds <2ms median wall-time to request preparation in non-simulated mode.
- Cost-savings: Measurable reduction in unexpected billing spikes for onboarding customers (target: 30% fewer first-month overages).

Non-goals
- Not a billing enforcement mechanism. It does not replace server-side billing controls.
- Not a full offline cost simulator for enterprise contract negotiation (that remains a server-side tool).

Functional requirements
1) Forecasting API (core):
   - forecastSessionCost(profileConfig) -> forecastReport
   - Accepts a profileConfig describing sequence length distribution, streaming flag, model variant, and embedding retention window.
   - Returns a forecastReport with expected token counts, per-token unit cost, total expected cost, and confidence bands (p10/p50/p90).
2) What-if simulation:
   - generateScenarios(baseProfile, variableRanges) -> scenarioReports[]
   - Support sweep over prompt length, temperature, and average response tokens.
3) SDK Policy hooks:
   - onForecastAbove(threshold, callback): allows client to surface preflight warnings or block a request in local dev sandboxes.
4) Lightweight offline mode:
   - Deterministic local estimator that runs without contacting Redwood network (uses locally cached performance and pricing profiles).
5) Telemetry and opt-in analytics:
   - Emit anonymized telemetry that maps forecast vs actual after requests are made (opt-in by default). Must include request fingerprint, model variant, forecasted and actual token counts, and an error code if model fallback occurred.
6) Reference UI/playbook:
   - A minimal React example page demonstrating preflight forecast and what-if experiments for a conversational route.

Non-functional requirements
- Language support: official SDKs in JavaScript/TypeScript and Python. Minimal reference in Go (CLI).
- Package size: JS bundle minified <45KB (core forecasting logic).
- Performance: local forecast path median 1.8ms on Node 18; network assisted forecast (<50ms) including shim.
- Security: SDK must not contain any secret keys; demos show tokenless sandboxing or use short-lived credentials.
- Licensing: BSD-3 or company-approved permissive license for sample code; production SDK published under Redwood terms.

Accuracy and data model
- Profiles: profileConfig fields: model_variant, prompt_length_distribution (mean/std or histogram), expected_user_turns, streaming(boolean), embedding_retention_days, expected_parallelism.
- Pricing model: SDK reads a pricing profile containing per-token generation and embedding costs, any per-request base fees, and variant multipliers. Pricing profiles are versioned.
- Performance impact: forecasts incorporate expected micro-batching efficiency based on expected concurrent sessions; default conservative multiplier applied for single-tenant sandboxes.

Telemetry, observability, and privacy
- Opt-in telemetry captures: sdk_version, forecast_id (uuid), model_variant, forecasted_tokens, actual_tokens, forecast_timestamp, request_timestamp, client_region (optional), scenario_label (optional).
- PII: telemetry shall not contain prompt text or any user data. SDK will hash request fingerprints and ensure telemetry only reports counts and labels.

SDK surface and example usage
- JavaScript (TypeScript) example snippet:

const sdk = new RedwoodDscSdk({ mode: 'offline', pricingProfile: '2026-04-v3' });
const profile = { model_variant: 'redwood-1-xl', prompt_length_distribution: { mean: 60, std: 20 }, expected_user_turns: 2, streaming: false, embedding_retention_days: 0 };
const report = await sdk.forecastSessionCost(profile);
console.log(report.total_cost, report.confidence.p90);

- ForecastReport schema (text table):
| field | description |
| forecast_id | uuid |
| total_cost | decimal USD estimated |
| tokens_input_est | estimated input tokens |
| tokens_output_est | estimated output tokens |
| per_token_unit | cents/token |
| confidence | p10/p50/p90 bands |

Reference configuration table (examples)
| Setting | Description | Example | Default |
| pricingProfile | Which pricing model to use | 2026-04-v3 | 2026-04-v3 |
| mode | offline | online | offline |
| cacheTTL | local pricing/perf cache TTL | 24h | 24h |
| conservativeMultiplier | multiplier applied to estimates | 1.15 | 1.15 |

Integration and rollout plan
1) Lab release (alpha) — Q3 2026 (internal + partner sandboxes)
   - Deliver JS/TS and Python alpha packages and reference React app.
   - Run a vehicle program with 3 integration partners to collect forecast vs actual telemetry.
2) Beta — Q4 2026
   - Incorporate telemetry-driven calibrations and pricing profile exports.
   - Add on-network pricing fetch and version pinning.
3) GA — Q1 2027
   - Publish official packages to npm/pypi, documentation, and Redwood Console integration (show forecast in onboarding panel).

Rollout milestones and success gates
- Gate A: Forecast accuracy (median error <= 15%) in partner pilots.
- Gate B: SDK stability: <2 critical bugs reported in partner integrations.
- Gate C: Documentation + Console embedding ready.

Operational considerations and ownership
- Product owner: Evelyn Chen (Product Manager)
- Engineering lead: Marcus Valdez (Developer Tools)
- SDK maintenance: eng-developer-experience
- Telemetry and calibrations: eng-platform (responsible for periodic pricing/perf profile updates)

Dependencies
- Up-to-date pricing profiles service and versioning (eng-platform).
- Performance profiles for model variants (eng-serving-runtime).
- Console onboarding panel integration (product + eng-platform).

Open questions and risks
- Pricing volatility: frequent changes to pricing could make cached profiles stale. Mitigation: default conservative multipliers and cache invalidation hooks.
- Accuracy for streaming workloads: estimating token-by-token streaming behavior has higher variance. Mitigation: require sampling and provide explicit p90 bands and guidance in docs.

Security and compliance notes
- SDK must not log or send prompt or user content. All telemetry uses hashed fingerprints.
- For restricted customers (confidential), shipping reference code is allowed but telemetry will remain default-off and must be approved by security.

Documentation and developer experience
- Publish a Getting Started guide, API reference, worked examples (conversational, embeddings, batch summarization), and a troubleshooting guide.
- Provide a CLI tool for bulk scenario simulation and CSV export to allow product managers to run scenario sweeps.

Appendix B — Example what-if sweep command (CLI)
redwood-dsc simulate --profile profile.yaml --sweep prompt_length:20,40,80 --out results.csv

Appendix C — Customer-facing messaging snippets for onboarding
- "Estimate per-session inference cost in your dev environment before you send production traffic."
- "Run what-if experiments to understand how prompt length and streaming change your unit costs."
